SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Painless swelling over left elbow noticed ~1 week ago; feels slightly warm and fluctuant; mild tenderness lateral to tip; full range of motion maintained. No prior episodes, trauma, or repetitive strain reported.
- Past medical history: Osteoarthritis (diagnosed by GP “a few years ago”).
- Medications: None routinely. (Ibuprofen 400 mg PO BID after food advised today; dose/route/frequency documented.)
- Social history: Desk-based job; runs 2–3×/week; otherwise active. No other social details provided.
- Allergies: Peanuts (reaction details not specified). No known drug allergies.

Objective:
- Video inspection of left elbow:
  • Visible swelling over olecranon region.  
  • Skin appears slightly dry; no marked erythema described.  
  • Area warmer than surrounding skin.  
  • Minimal tenderness adjacent to olecranon; tip itself non-tender.  
  • Full active movement demonstrated.  
- No vitals recorded.
- Planned investigations: Blood tests (inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, uric acid/gout screen).

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left elbow swelling
   - Assessment: Likely olecranon bursitis (non-septic).
   - Differential diagnosis: Septic bursitis/arthritis, gout, inflammatory arthropathy.
   - Investigations planned: Blood panel as above; arrange form to be mailed to patient; anticipate results ~6 days after sampling.
   - Treatment planned: Ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily with food; discontinue if heartburn occurs.
   - Follow-up: Patient to book video or face-to-face review after blood results available. Advise urgent contact if elbow becomes very red, markedly painful, or swelling spreads (concern for septic arthritis).

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected elements: Vital signs; detailed reaction to peanut allergy; smoking/alcohol history; medication reconciliation beyond OTC use.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational filler, no significant inaudible sections.
